messages:
jen (customer): Hey team — we're seeing streaming responses from the Redwood API drop after ~60s. Client sees a partial JSON chunk and then connection closes. This is happening from our prod app behind ALB -> nginx. Any ideas?

jake (support): sorry you're hitting this, jen. Do you have a curl repro or a HAR? Also which route/model and whether you're using the /v1/streams or the websocket shim?

jen (customer): Using the SSE endpoint /v1/streams with text/event-stream. Route: chat-completions, model: openllm-small. Here's a quick curl we used:

```
curl -v -N 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=openllm-small'
```

We get the first few events, then nothing, then connection reset. Reconnect shows remaining content but duplicates some tokens.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks — that pattern smells like an intermediate proxy idle timeout or response buffering. ALB default idle timeout is 60s. Can you confirm ALB idle timeout or whether there are any rate-limiting front doors (Cloudflare)?

jen (customer): confirmed ALB timeout is 60s. We have nginx behind ALB doing TLS termination and passing to internal forwarding to your endpoint (via private egress). No Cloudflare.

ingrid (infra): two quick checks: 1) Is nginx using proxy_buffering on? 2) Are you using HTTP/1.1 keepalive and chunked transfer? If nginx buffers to disk it will hold until buffer fills or upstream finishes.

jen (customer): nginx conf excerpt (simplified):
```
proxy_pass http://internal-redwood;
proxy_buffering on;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
```

jen (customer): we just realized our nginx default was proxy_buffering on and timeouts 60s.

jake (support): yep, that explains it. For SSE/streaming you want to disable buffering and extend read timeout. Two quick fixes:

- For nginx: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s;`
- For ALB: increase idle timeout to >300s (or to match your expected session life) — ALB default 60s will cut idle connections.

maria (eng-runtime): and when testing, use `curl -N` (we saw you do) because `-N` disables curl buffering. Also include `-H 'Connection: keep-alive'` to ensure the proxy sees the right header. Example reproducer we use:

```
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Connection: keep-alive' 
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=openllm-small' > out.txt
```

Watch the bytes in real time: `tail -f out.txt` while streaming.

ingrid (infra): additional note for ALB + nginx stacks: ALB will health-check and may terminate connections when it believes the backend is idle. If you can't increase ALB idle timeout, you can enable periodic keepalive heartbeats from the client or server-side SSE comment lines (`: ping\n\n`) to keep the wire active. Redwood's streaming runtime will send periodic pings when configured, but client proxies sometimes strip those.

jen (customer): After changing nginx to `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_read_timeout 3600s` and bumping ALB idle to 300s, the stream stayed open and content arrived progressively. Nice. One oddity: some extra blank lines and occasional duplicate tokens on reconnect. Thoughts?

maria (eng-runtime): duplicates on reconnect are expected if client reconnects and server retries last chunk; you should use `Last-Event-ID` handling on the client to dedupe, or idempotency tokens in the event payload. We'll also add a server-side trailing event id so reconnections can request resume.

ingrid (infra): duplicates can also come from buffering layers — if proxy retried a request after timeout the server may re-play. Check ALB access logs for multiple sequential requests from the same client IP around the disconnect time.

ops-bot: Incident check: no platform-side errors or restarts from 1792000000-1792002000.

jake (support): great that config change helped. Action items:
- jen: keep the nginx/ALB changes in place and monitor for 24h.
- maria: follow up on adding a resumable event id for SSE streams (ticket).
- ingrid: add KB blurb for "SSE behind ALB + nginx" with recommended settings.

jen (customer): thanks all — will report back if anything else shows up. Really appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

maria (eng-runtime): happy to help. If you hit Cloudflare in the future, note that Cloudflare will buffer responses for certain plans; there are Cloudflare-specific toggles (disable response buffering / set origin to bypass) — ping us before flipping that so we can coordinate.

jake (support): closing the thread for now; reopen if it recurs.
